card.name: Deodhani
card.era: Traditional; tied to Manasa and Kamakhya worship
card.tagline: Assamese trance dance of the serpent goddess Manasa
card.profile: Deodhani is a ritual trance-dance of Assam associated with the worship of the serpent goddess Manasa and the goddess Kamakhya (AssamInfo). The word means 'a woman possessed by a deity'; female deodhanis (and, at the Kamakhya temple, male deodhas) enter possession states believed to channel the goddess, dancing vigorously with rapid head rotations, open flowing hair and serpent-like movements to the beat of drums, often enacting Behula's dance from the Manasa legend. It is performed during the Deodhani/Manasa Puja festival, especially the three-day festival at Kamakhya in August, and in Than rituals in Kamrup, Darrang and Sonitpur (Burley 2019; AssamInfo).
card.insight: Scholar Mikel Burley's peer-reviewed study (Religions of South Asia, 2019) documents the Kamakhya 'Dance of the Deodhas', noting devotees' claims that performers are possessed by several ferocious goddesses amid blood sacrifice (White Rose Research Online).
card.image_significance: Trance dance of the snake goddess. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Assam (Bodo-Kachari), India.
